newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close down on strike concerns.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close down on strike concerns.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed lower across the board Monday in weak trade as the market nervously awaited a 12-hour national work stoppage set for Wednesday, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index fell 2.08 percent to 9,238.99, as 31 stocks fell, three rose and eight closed flat.
The Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), Venezuela's largest union, has called the work stoppage to pressure private companies to raise wages.
"All indicators of volume and number of trades fell because there are no investors. The sellers are holding back a bit and there are few buyers," one broker said.
A total of just 2.544 billion bolivars ($5.1 million) in 776 trades exchange hands.
Brokers said the underlying tendency of the market remained upward.

"We have to wait to see how Wednesday's strike goes. If everything goes smoothly the market will resume its rise but if the atmosphere continues to be tense the market will continue falling," another broker.
Among leading stocks the only one to post gains was Ceramica Carabobo which rose 5.00 bolivars to 570.00 bolivars.

Benchmark Electricidad de Caracas lost 14.00 bolivars to 804.00 bolivars, telephone company CANTV fell 38.00 bolivars to 3,005.00 bolivars and steel company Sivensa slipped 6.75 bolivars to 268.75 bolivars.
